Why inventory can rise while service still falls

More stock can spread uncertainty across the network without addressing its source.

Illustrative scenario analysis · 6–8 minute read
This article illustrates a recurring supply-chain pattern and the JourneyIQ Supply Chain Diagnostic method. It does not describe a named client, completed engagement or verified customer outcome.

The situation

A business adds buffer and still experiences shortages because aggregate stock does not show whether the right material is available at the right place and time.

Three patterns

Variable supplier lead time, outdated planning parameters and material waiting for documentation can create the same high-inventory, low-service symptom.

From stock position to journey

Link demand, order, commitment, shipment, receipt and availability events, then segment by material and operating pattern.

The decision sequence

Intervene where variability enters before testing stock-policy changes. The evidence may point to supplier recovery, planning, release or allocation rules.
